messages:
priya: Quick sync — finalizing KEK rotation playbook for envelope encryption across AWS/GCP/Azure. Two asks: (1) automatic periodic rotation vs manual rewrap by ops, (2) required RBAC + audit checks for safety.

Derek: Prefer auto for routine rotations but manual-first for initial rollouts. Rewrap at scale needs careful controls.

maya: Envelope reminder: we only rewrap DEKs under a new KEK version. Steps: create new KEK version -> rewrap DEK -> swap metadata. Avoid touching ciphertext payloads until canary passes.

elaine: Cloud differences: AWS has ReEncrypt (server-side). GCP lacks a direct ReEncrypt API — typical approach is decrypt/encrypt inside a trusted service. Azure has wrapKey/unwrapKey.

priya: Proposed plan: t0 create new KEK version in each cloud, provision service account, run canary rewrap on small subset, monitor audit logs/errors, then scale with rate limits. Who owns canary selection?

Derek: Rate limits: start 100 objs/min first hour, 500-1k/min next day, then ramp. Backoff on 5xx or KMS quota errors. Per-shard cursors so we can resume.

maya: Add ciphertext header versioning to support v1/v2 during migration. Header fields: version, kek_uri, kek_version, wrap_alg, wrapped_key, rewrap_status.

elaine: Suggest storing rewrap_status in metadata (pending/in_progress/done/failed) so jobs are idempotent. Pseudocode example:
```
if header.version == "v1": // legacy decrypt
elif header.version == "v2": // new flow
```

jim: RBAC: create dedicated principal kms-rewraper@ with least privilege: AWS kms:ReEncrypt on specific KEK ARNs, GCP cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt/useToDecrypt scoped to key resource, Azure wrapKey/unwrapKey on specific vault keys. No broad kms:*.

priya: Audit requirements: forward KMS ops to SIEM (CloudTrail, Cloud Audit Logs, Azure Diagnostic). Alert when rewrap/decrypt calls originate from unexpected principals or regions.

ops-bot: Deploy checklist: 1) new KEK created 2) service account provisioned 3) canary dataset picked 4) audit sink configured 5) canary job deployed 6) dashboards + alerts enabled

Derek: Vulnerability triage: on suspected KEK compromise, emergency rotate: create new KEK version, run prioritized dry-run rewrap on high-risk records, rotate rewrap service credentials, then full rewrap. Keep old wrapped_keys until verification.

maya: Cost note: KMS API calls bill per-call. Add cost estimate for million rewraps. Include billing alerts to avoid surprises.

elaine: Backwards compat: keep old KEK versions readable (disabled for encrypt) until all records show rewrap_status=done. Only schedule key deletion after cross-check.

priya: Incident playbook: feature flag to freeze writers or force kek_version=latest during emergency, and a rollback path to resume using old KEK if needed.

jim: Monitoring/metrics: rewrap_success_count, rewrap_error_count, rewrap_latency_ms, ciphertext_version_distribution, kek_access_by_principal. PagerDuty on error_rate spike or unexpected principal access.

elaine: Canary failure modes: permission denied, network timeouts, corrupted wrapped_key. On corruption, mark record failed and do not delete old wrapped_key; escalate to SRE/security.

maya: Implementation notes: rewrap workers should stream tasks with idempotency_token and persist cursor in DB so job can resume without duplicating work.

elaine: Example idempotent API:
```
POST /internal/rewrap
{ "record_id": "...", "target_kek": "...", "idempotency_key": "..." }
```
Worker calls KMS (ReEncrypt or decrypt/encrypt) then updates rewrap_status.

priya: Timeline suggestion: canary 48h, evaluate metrics and logs, then 1 week gradual rollout across regions. Allow fast emergency path for high-severity compromises.

Derek: DR note: if old KEK is disabled prematurely, revert requires backups of wrapped_keys and offline copy of KEK material if policy allows. Document recovery steps.

maya: Oncall runbook snippet: how to pause pipeline (/internal/pause-rewrap), how to inspect last-processed cursor, how to resume with dry-run mode.

elaine: I'll own SIEM queries for detecting anomalous KEK access. Example query (CloudTrail):
```
eventName = ReEncrypt OR eventName = Decrypt
| filter userIdentity.principal != "arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/kms-rewraper"
| stats count() by userIdentity.principal, awsRegion
```

priya: Any blockers? I’ll draft the playbook this afternoon and post for review. Need confirmation on GCP perms mapping and cost numbers.

jim: I'll validate GCP IAM bindings and run a quick permission check script against a staging KEK.

Derek: Also confirm billing alerts and add a hard throttle to job to stop if cost threshold exceeded.

maya: I'll add idempotency and cursor logic to the rewrap worker PR.

elaine: I'll finalize audit forwarding and dashboard panels.

priya: Thanks all — tagging reviewers. :thumbsup:
